conviction_note: Ten small sourced items that roughly offset (findings sum -0.25): the intra-quarter negatives (NIM flat in Q3, $20m Stellantis lease loss, softer used-car prices, rising deposit and CD rates after the Sept 16 Fed hike, higher industry hail losses, an AOCI hit to book value) are almost all public and arrived alongside two downgrades, a cut Wells EPS of $1.25 and a 17% fall since the last print. Against them: wider industry auto loan spreads, strong used-vehicle demand and a call-heavy option book. The consensus EPS is disputed ($1.25-$1.47), so p_up sits at 50 and the scaled number is 0. abs_move 5.0 sits between the 7.16% option-implied move and the 2.39% median reaction, raised from the median because the Q4 NIM path under rising rates and early 2027 credit colour are new this print.
bar: Disputed, so every size is capped. Consensus Q3 2026 adj EPS is about $1.33 (Investing.com/Ortex preview cluster, https://ng.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/ally-financial-earnings-loom-as-analysts-cut-forecasts-93CH-2743853), but other sources give $1.36 (Tiger, https://www.itiger.com/news/1168760375, 2026-10-13), $1.43 (Earnings Whispers) and $1.47 (TickerLeague, range $1.30-$1.67). Wells Fargo cut its own estimate to $1.25 against a $1.42 consensus on 2026-09-30 (https://www.ad-hoc-news.de/boerse/news/corporate-news/ally-financial-stock-heads-toward-october-20-earnings-after-target-cut/70225592). Revenue consensus is about $2.29-2.30bn. Company guide: FY26 NIM 3.6-3.7%, retail auto NCO 1.8-2.0%, Q3 NIM roughly flat QoQ, about $20m Q3 Stellantis lease losses (Barclays, 2026-09-15). Q2 actual was $1.21 adj EPS, NIM 3.63%, retail auto NCO 1.57%.
positioning_check: Short interest just over 5% of free float, up 21% over the past month (step-up around Oct 8), about 4 days to cover, borrow 0.28% and loose (Ortex, as of 2026-10-17, https://ortex.news/articles/190800/ally-financial-heads-into-q3-print-with-shorts-building-and-street-cutting-targets). FINRA via Curved Trading: 12.9M shares, 4.8 days to cover at 2026-08-14 (https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/ally/short-interest/). Not a crowded short. Baseline: 25-delta skew +5.0 vol points (downside paid, moderate), but put/call open interest 0.25 (call-heavy) and Ortex reports call-tilted flow (P/C 0.80). ATM IV 36.8% against 17.9% 20-day realised vol, event-implied move 7.16% against a 2.39% median historical reaction, so options price a much bigger move than this name usually makes. Spot $37.41, -6.2% over 20 days, 4% above the 52-week low and 21% below the high.

findings.finding: At Barclays on 2026-09-15 CFO Hutchinson said Q3 NIM would be roughly flat QoQ (Q2 was 3.63%), a step back from the Q2-call view that Q3 would benefit from June deposit cuts. He also flagged about $20m of Q3 lease residual losses on recalled Stellantis vehicles, about $0.05/share after tax, persisting through 2026. Both sit inside the reaffirmed FY guide (NIM 3.6-3.7%, retail auto NCO 1.8-2.0%) and the stock fell 2.7% that day.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: July 2026: a $0.01-0.04 miss attributed to provisions/credit costs, -2.39%. April 2026: a large EPS beat ($1.11 vs ~$0.94), +8.1%. The stock moves on NIM and credit lines.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: it was public, the stock dropped 2.7% on the day and Wells Fargo built it into its $1.25 estimate. What remains open is whether consensus near $1.33-1.47 fully absorbed it. A $1.43 consensus would mean it did not, so the dispersion in the bar is itself the residual risk.
findings.independence: Same remarks are reported in MarketBeat/Yahoo on 2026-09-19 (https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/ally-financial-reaffirms-guidance-margin-150159380.html). That is the same event, not independent.

findings.finding: The Street cut ahead of the print. Wells Fargo downgraded to Equal Weight on 2026-09-30 (PT $55 to $42, Q3 EPS to $1.25 vs $1.42 consensus). Morgan Stanley downgraded on 2026-10-12 (PT $55 to $43, citing higher funding costs and a less favourable credit backdrop). JPMorgan cut its PT to $43, and RBC, Raymond James, TD Cowen, UBS and Citi trimmed targets to the low $50s. The stock is down about 17% since the July print, at $37.41 versus a $35.92 52-week low.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The baseline's 2025-10-17 print came after a pre-print sell-off and moved +3.56%. April 2026, after a lowered bar, +8.1%. July 2026, after a run-up to a $47 high, -2.39%.
findings.why_not_priced: The cuts themselves are priced (wire copy). The open question is whether the lowered bar ($1.25 at the bear end) means an in-line print plus reaffirmed guide gets bought. If the market had fully reset, the skew would not still be +5 and the event-implied move would not be 3x the median reaction. Capped small because the consensus is disputed between $1.25 and $1.47.
findings.independence: Wells Fargo detail from ad-hoc-news (https://www.ad-hoc-news.de/boerse/news/corporate-news/ally-financial-stock-heads-toward-october-20-earnings-after-target-cut/70225592). Morgan Stanley reasoning from Goldesel (https://goldesel.de/aktien/news/ally-financial-aktie-morgan-stanley-senkt-rating-wegen-zinsrisiken). Both are secondary.

findings.finding: The Manheim index fell 1.1% MoM in September 2026 to 205.9, -0.6% YoY, with steeper-than-seasonal depreciation. Cox cut its 2026 year-end forecast to +0.2% YoY from +2% in July, citing record diesel, rising rates and weaker consumer sentiment. Ally had credited H1 credit outperformance partly to used-vehicle values and expects them to normalise in H2, so recoveries and lease remarketing gains shrink and the 1.8-2.0% NCO guide and 2027 credit commentary face pressure.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: July 2026: credit costs/provision drove a -2.39% day. Used-car values are the lever management itself named for H1 credit outperformance.
findings.why_not_priced: It is public and broad. Transmission into Ally's Q4 NCO and residual commentary is not yet confirmed by the company. If priced, management's 'normalisation' language would already be read as a guide cut, but consensus still carries EPS growth. This is a proxy, so it is filed small.
findings.independence: Cox September page (https://www.coxautoinc.com/insights/manheim-used-vehicle-value-index-september-2026-trends/) is the same publisher. Morgan Stanley's 'less favorable credit backdrop' (Goldesel) points the same way.

findings.finding: Wells Fargo's 3Q26 results deck (2026-10-13) shows Auto revenue +33% YoY and +7% QoQ 'on higher loan balances and wider loan spreads', auto originations $10.1bn vs $8.8bn a year earlier, and average auto loans $58.8bn vs $44.8bn. Consumer NCOs fell to 70bp despite 'higher auto net loan charge-offs' QoQ. For prime auto this means spreads are widening (supporting Ally's originated yields) while losses rise seasonally, and a large bank competitor is growing hard.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No direct history. Ally's April +8.1% came on yield/NIM strength.
findings.why_not_priced: It is a peer print after Ally last spoke (2026-09-15) and is not in any Ally preview. The bear case (MS) says auto yields are 'relatively stable' while funding rises, and a peer showing wider auto spreads cuts against that. Mixed sign: spreads up is positive, higher auto NCOs and a competitor growing loans 31% are offsets. Proxy, so it is small.
findings.independence: Ally itself said at Barclays that originated yields should improve on Q2/Q3 pricing actions and competition was favourable (investing.com transcript, 2026-09-15).

findings.finding: Ally raised deposit pricing around the 2026-09-16 Fed hike (to 3.75-4.00%). Five CD rates went up on 2026-09-09 and eight on 2026-09-22, with the 18-month CD at 4.25%. Online savings went from 3.00% to 3.10% APY by 2026-10-13, a ~40% beta on the 25bp hike against the 69-70% beta management cited on the way down. Funding costs are rising into Q4 against management's aim to exit 2026 at or above 3.7% NIM.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: July 2026 NIM 3.63% (+11bp QoQ) with a small miss, -2.39%. April's +8.1% came with NIM expansion.
findings.why_not_priced: Deposit rate changes are on Ally's own website but are not aggregated in any preview. MS's downgrade argues funding pressure generically, without numbers. If priced, consensus would already have cut Q4 NIM, but the bulk of estimates still assume NIM expansion. The 10bp OSA move is modest, a partial offset that cuts the size. Snippet-level CD data; the OSA history is single-source.
findings.independence: depositaccounts.com forum posts 'Ally Rate Changes as of 9-9-2026' and '9-22-2026' (https://www.depositaccounts.com/community/promos/63503-ally-rate-changes-9222026.html, snippet_only, page 403). MonitorBankRates 2026-10-07 shows 18-month CD 4.25%.

findings.finding: Q3 2026 severe convective storm (hail/wind) losses ran well above last year. Travelers Q3 cat losses were $538m vs $302m a year earlier, mainly 'severe wind and hail storms in multiple states', and Allstate Q3 cat losses were $1.65bn pre-tax. Ally Insurance (~$490m quarterly revenue, dealer inventory physical-damage exposure) carries weather losses, so a modest Q3 insurance drag is likely.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No baseline evidence that the insurance line has moved the stock. It is a small segment.
findings.why_not_priced: Ally previews do not mention weather. This is macro-to-company transmission Ally has not confirmed, and dealer-lot geography differs from homeowners' books. Proxy, small; it is net of the rest of the company (auto finance and corporate finance dominate earnings).

findings.finding: Rates rose in Q3 2026 (Fed hike 2026-09-16). Wells Fargo reported its AOCI decline 'driven by the impact of higher interest rates' cut CET1 by 38bp QoQ, so Ally's AFS securities AOCI, and with it tangible book value per share, likely fell in Q3.
findings.why_not_priced: It is a mechanical consequence of public rates, and Ally's opt-out keeps it out of regulatory CET1. Filed small because a TBV dip is visible in the release but rarely moves a name on its own.
findings.independence: Shares the Wells deck with the Wells auto finding, but uses a different line of it (capital slide vs CBL slide).

findings.finding: On 2026-09-09 Ally priced $750m of 5.525% fixed-to-floating senior notes due 2030 (callable 2029, then SOFR+117bp) at par. Use of proceeds is not stated in the term sheet. It reads as routine unsecured refinancing at a tight spread that supports a still-growing book (average earning asset guide raised to +3-5%).
findings.why_not_priced: Public and immaterial. Asked what the money buys: it funds asset growth the company raised guidance for, so the sign is non-negative. Filed for completeness.

findings.finding: CarMax's Q2 FY27 (quarter to 2026-08-31, reported 2026-09-29) showed revenue +19.5% to $7.9bn, EPS $1.16 vs ~$0.73 expected, and CarMax Auto Finance income +32.1% to $135.6m. That points to strong used-vehicle retail demand and auto-finance economics through August, supporting Ally's application/origination volume (Q2 originations +21%, record 4.6m applications).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Ally's Q2 originations surge came with a -2.39% day, because credit costs dominated. Volume alone has not paid.
findings.why_not_priced: It is a peer print after Ally last spoke, but CarMax's quarter ends a month before Ally's and volume is not what the stock trades on. Proxy, small.
findings.independence: Wells Fargo auto originations +15% YoY (Wells 3Q26 deck), a different document.

findings.finding: Positioning into the print is not crowded and leans to calls. Short interest is just over 5% of float (up 21% in a month), about 4 days to cover, borrow 0.28%. The baseline shows put/call open interest of 0.25 and Ortex reports call-tilted flow (P/C 0.80), while the 25-delta skew is +5 (downside paid) and the event-implied move of 7.16% is 3x the 2.39% median reaction.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The max reaction in 7 prints is 8.1% (April 2026), median 2.39%. Implied vol prices a far larger move than history.
findings.why_not_priced: Shorts added about 21% into the print on a name already down 17%. Covering on an in-line print is a mechanism, but at 5% of float it is a small one. Rich implied vol relative to history means option sellers expect less than priced. Mixed sign, small.
findings.independence: Shares the Ortex article with the Street-cuts finding (different facts, same document). Short-interest series from Curved Trading/FINRA (https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/ally/short-interest/).

baseline_tension: Mixed. The intra-quarter negatives (rates, used-car prices, deposit costs) agree with the +5 put skew and the -6% 20-day run-up and are largely priced through two downgrades and estimate cuts. The call-heavy open interest, a stock 4% off its 52-week low and evidence of wider auto spreads cut the other way, so the net is near zero.
lessons_applied: Rule 6 (bar disputed, $1.25-$1.47 across sources): capped the bar-dependent Street-cuts/lowered-bar positioning finding from +1.0 to +0.6, and moved p_up from 52 to 50, so expected_move goes from +0.2 to 0.0
Rule 6 (inside what the company guided): Barclays NIM-flat/Stellantis finding moved toward 0, -0.3 to -0.2
Rule 5 (proxy, filed small, not dropped): Manheim, Wells Fargo, CarMax, weather and AOCI items left at their small draft sizes; no change
Rule 4 (financing is a question): senior notes already signed non-negative after asking what the money buys; no change
Rule 7: short interest checked before negatives (5% float, ~4 DTC, not crowded); no change to negatives
